Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testLoopingOptionLookAlike2` tries to parse command-line arguments containing multiple identical tokens "testfile.txt". The test expects an OptionException with a message about an unexpected token.

From the `Parser.parse` method, arguments are copied into a list that is iterated to process options. The processing loop relies on the `Group.canProcess` and `Group.process` methods to consume arguments.

Examining `GroupImpl.process`, command line tokens are iterated, and options mapped are processed if found. Otherwise, the logic checks if an argument looks like an option or is anonymous, attempting to process accordingly. The iterator is cautiously handled to avoid infinite loops.

In option processing, the `ArgumentImpl.process` delegates to `processValues`, which attempts to consume multiple argument values up to a maximum count. During parsing, if the next token looks like an option, it breaks to avoid consuming unintended tokens, causing the iterator to backtrack.

The test setup uses two mandatory arguments (input and output), wrapped in a `SourceDestArgument`, grouped as an option in the parser. The parser tries to parse four identical "testfile.txt" arguments which exceed the allowed number for the option combination.

The exception is thrown when the parser encounters an unexpected argument it cannot associate with any option or anonymous argument. The error message "Unexpected testfile.txt while processing " matches the failing test's expectation.

The current bug report mentions issues when an option has a default argument value and a second value is supplied on the command line, causing parsing failure because the command line already has a value for the option. This aligns with the error, showing default values in the command line persist and prevent additional values from being accepted. 

The problem likely stems from `processValues` or `addValue` in `WriteableCommandLine`, which may not allow overriding or adding values when defaults are present, blocking proper parsing of multiple values or repeated arguments.

In conclusion, the failure is due to argument default values in the option preventing the command line parser from accepting multiple input arguments, triggering an unexpected token exception during parsing. The root cause is the handling of argument values in presence of defaults and enforcing maximum argument counts in `processValues`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
